data.name: Kishansh
data.gender_notes: Kishansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kishansh is derived from two Sanskrit words: 'Kishan' meaning 'Lord' and 'Sh' meaning 'Earth'. This name is associated with the deity Vishnu, who is often depicted as the preserver of the universe and the nurturer of all beings. The name Kishansh is believed to bestow upon its bearer the virtues of strength, nurturing qualities, and the ability to preserve and protect.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name of Vishnu, the preserver of the universe
data.etymology: Kishansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kishansh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Kishansh Suri was a Jain merchant who established the Suri Dynasty in the 16th century in Bengal, India. The Suri dynasty ruled from 1540 to 1636 AD.

Kishansh was also the name of a legendary king in ancient Indian texts, believed to have ruled in the 12th century BC during the Mahabharata era. He was the ruler of the kingdom of Kishkindha and a devotee of Lord Hanuman.
